fixes.explanation: The king isn't in this verse, baker. Verse 14 says, "Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD." Prudent means careful and sensible, someone who thinks before she acts. Houses and wealth get handed down through fathers, but the verse puts a prudent wife in a different column, from the LORD.

Nope, this one's true, baker. Verse 4 says, "Wealth attracts many friends…" Solomon isn't cheering it on, he's just watching, and I think it stings a little. Money walks into the room and suddenly everybody's your best friend, yet the verse says a poor man is deserted by his friend.

Elders aren't in this verse, baker. Verse 14 says, "Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD." A father can pass down a house and money, but a prudent wife is from the LORD. I think that's worth slowing down for, friend, because some things can't be handed down like a house.

The king isn't in this verse, baker. Verse 17 says, "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender." When you are kind to the poor, the verse counts it as lending to the LORD. He is the One who repays. So it isn't a gift to a king, it's a loan with the LORD as the One who pays it back.

This one's true, baker. Verse 17 says, "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender." It's like handing a friend twenty bucks, except here the One who pays you back is the LORD, and the verse says He will. Picking False would pull that promise right out of the verse.

This one is true, baker. Verse 23 says, "The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm." The verse goes step by step: the fear of the LORD leads to life, and that life rests content, without visitation from harm. Picking False would cut that chain, because Solomon ties the rest to the fear of the LORD.

That would be the opposite, baker. Verse 27 says, "If you cease to hear instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge." Learning is where hearing instruction takes you, but this verse is about someone who quits listening. Quit listening and you drift away from the words of knowledge, like a boat with the rope untied. That's why the verse works as a warning to keep listening.
